# SF five-minute range-repair regression

The original SF run used SDK
`99c14495685f160019e10340ea6f0de6418a65b9` and ended after three model calls
with a clarification, without an admitted plan. The selected combination's
legal planning range was **336–14044 seconds**, above the 330-second acceptance
ceiling at its minimum. The user had no confirmed dose parameter; the chair's
fixed 3 sets / 12 reps / 30-second rests are catalog constraints.

The source diagnosis is the read-only SF file
`Sport-Helper-coach-ui-kit/docs/reports/sdk-ui-kit-plus51-sdk99c1449/offline-five-minute-diagnosis/`.
`manifest.json` binds its recorded protocol, profile, pre-draft state and the
original real-capture SHA-256. The source capture remains external and unchanged.
Only the exact user text, tool arguments and structured facts needed by the
regression are included; there are no credentials or private model reasoning.

- `recorded-tool-batches.json` preserves the original three tools-only response
  batches and arguments in their original order. IDs are those uniquely
  regenerated by the published offline diagnostic, not asserted original HTTP IDs.
- `pre-draft-state.json` is the diagnostic's actual public-protocol state just
  before call three. Its original 32 seen action IDs are retained.
- `catalog.json` retains those 32 drills in original catalog order. It is built
  from the immutable SDK pack's `toAiCatalog()` and the same SF `_planningCadence`
  projection, including existing video paths and execution cycles. Every one of
  the five selected raw drill objects was checked against the diagnostic's
  `selectedDefinitions` for structural equality. No dose ranges were changed.
- `execution-rhythms.json` retains the diagnostic's exact five runtime rhythms,
  including self-paced status, authored phases and lead.
- `baseline-receipt.json` retains the old handled clarification receipt, rather
  than rewriting it into a new success.

The root SDK test replays the original three batches over a real `CoachAgent`.
It then appends an explicitly **synthetic FakeLlmClient continuation** that reads
the new repair receipt, removes the suggested chair action and submits a new
draft followed by `show_plan`. It proves local retry/control-flow and delivery
without asking the user. It is not another real model sample or a claim that the
historical provider generated the repaired plan. Network access is disabled.

The repaired offline result is a 291-second planning estimate and a 292-second
Trainer timeline with SF's 10-second preparation and authored lead. The original
chair is self-paced, so the old 336-second minimum is a planning lower bound,
not a guaranteed automatic execution time or device measurement. The repaired
selection drops that manual action; its remaining rep actions are counted.

The same SDK regression also reuses the unchanged HipLab third-turn fixture
under `packages/ugk_trainer/test/fixtures/hiplab/fit-all-blocks/`. Its source
pre-draft state is explicitly reconstructed there. A synthetic continuation
reconfirms the replacement operation for the replayed turn before using the
original draft structure and delivering it; the old version remains unchanged.
Its card remains 309 seconds, and its authored/voice-aware Trainer timeline is
323 seconds including the original 15-second preparation.

No source App, SDK fitter search order, original capture, catalog bytes, dose
limits, cadence, preparation time or device was modified to make these cases pass.
